By Advs. Smt.Deepa Narayanan
 Smt.Asha Mariam Mathews
 Sri Sujai Sathyan

THIS OP (FAMILY COURT) HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON  09.12.2024, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 2024:KER:92866 OP (FC) NO. 171 OF 2021  -2- A.P.Basheer vs Noushad P.V on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152990964/
1  JUDGMENT Devan Ramachandran, J.
The order of the learned Family Court, Tirur, in I.A.No.2/2020 in O.P.No.558/2020 has been called into question before us by the petitioners.

2. The petitioners are the maternal grandparents of a young boy by name Muhammed Nihal; and they seem to be aggrieved by the impugned order because the respondent, who is the father of the child, has been given his interim custody on certain days of a month, as also during holidays.

They say that the child is unwilling and reluctant to go to his father, particularly because they believe that he is guilty of their daughter (the child's mother) having committed suicide in the year 2018.

The petitioners point out that the respondent has been chargesheeted by the Police, after investigation, under the provisions of Sections 304B, 498A and 306 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and that trial against him is pending.

They assert that, therefore, in such scenario, the order of the learned Family Court, sending the child away with the respondent, is not only deleterious to him, but contrary to the principles of custodianship.

4. We have heard Sri.S.Sreekumar (Chelur)
- learned counsel for the petitioners; and Sri.Sujai Sathyan - learned counsel for the respondent.

5. Sri.Sujai Sathyan argued that the afore contentions of the petitioners are untenable 2024:KER:92866 OP (FC) NO. 171 OF 2021 because, the child has been heavily tutored and told fake stories about his father, namely his client, on a regular basis.

He explained that the child has already spent two or three days with his father in the year 2020 and that he was extremely happy to be with him; and therefore, that the present order does not suffer from any error.

6. However, Sri.S.Sreekumar (Chelur) - learned counsel for the petitioners, contended that, even when the child was with the respondent - father, for two or three days in the year 2020, he was heavily traumatized because he was not treated well and his mind was tried to be corrupted by him for confutative basis.

He argued that, when the child is wholly unwilling to go with the father, it was improper 2024:KER:92866 OP (FC) NO. 171 OF 2021 for the learned Family Court to have allowed the latter the interim custody of the former.

7. We notice from the impugned order that the learned Family Court has decided it on the premise that the bonding between the respondent and the child has been lost because of lack of contact for a long period of time.
It also referred to its earlier order, to state that it was found, at that time, that the child was happy to be with the father.
It further noticed that the child was with the father during a period of four days in the year 2020; and hence that it is unfair for the child to be denied paternal company and custody.

It thus allowed the father to be in the custody of the child during certain days,

2 as an interim arrangement.

sentences.text: 8. It is without contest that 2024:KER:92866 OP (FC) NO. 171 OF 2021 O.P.No.558/2020 was filed by the respondent/father herein seeking permanent custody of the child.
However, in I.A.No.2/2020 - from which the impugned order arises - the respondent/father sought only interim custody.
This has now been granted.
9. The parties were before us today personally, along with the child.

10. We interacted with the child, who showed extreme fear towards the respondent; and explained,
saying that he believes that his father is responsible for his mother's death.
However, he was unable to explain how he came to be under that impression, except saying that he saw certain written notes which his maternal grandmother showed him.
11. We made an attempt to allow the 2024:KER:92866 OP (FC) NO. 171 OF 2021 respondent to be with the child in our Chambers, by making them sit next to each other on the visitor's sofa.
However, the child remained in such a situation only for less than a minute and then ran away to his grandparents, who were waiting outside the Chambers.

He was crying inconsolably; and it is thus,
prima facie, obvious that he does not want to be even in the presence of his father, much less talk to him.

12. One, therefore, wonders how the order of the learned Family Court can be implemented, though we cannot find fault with it in having given interim custody of a child to his father because, in normal circumstances, such a bonding is essential, if not imperative.

13. In the case at hand, when the child exhibits deep fear towards his father and when 2024:KER:92866 OP (FC) NO. 171 OF 2021 we are told that the latter is facing trial in the criminal case, it is not available to us to assure him that his father is innocent, since the evidence in that regard is yet to be established.

14. Indubitably, therefore, it would not be possible for us to confirm the impugned order at this time, though the learned Family Court can take a final decision appositely because, the Original Petition is still pending before it.

15. In the meanwhile, perhaps the trial in the criminal case against the father would also be concluded, which would give some amount of clarity and assurance to the child, if the former is to be finally acquitted.

16. As matters now stand, the child seems 2024:KER:92866 OP (FC) NO. 171 OF 2021 to have deep apprehensions against his father - perhaps to a larger extent on account of the inputs that have been given to him or obtained by him - but when he exhibits the same, it would not be possible to send him with the father, against his wishes.
A.P.Basheer vs Noushad P.V on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152990964/
3 17. We are also persuaded to the afore because of the bail conditions imposed against the respondent.
Any action of the father to force him or otherwise can even be construed to be in violation of the same.
This, however, does not appear to have been looked into by the learned Family Court while issuing the impugned order.

In the afore circumstances, we deem it necessary to intervene; and therefore, allow this Original Petition and set aside Ext.P6;
2024:KER:92866 OP (FC) NO. 171 OF 2021 however, leaving every liberty to the respondent - father to invoke his remedies before the learned Family Court in the pending Original Petition.
Sd/-
DEVAN RAMACHANDRAN JUDGE Sd/-
